definition: A point in a model's loss landscape where the loss is lower than at all nearby points, but not necessarily the lowest possible loss overall (the global minimum).
details: In high-dimensional deep learning loss landscapes, research suggests that poor local minima are less of a practical problem than once feared, with saddle points and landscape geometry often mattering more for optimization difficulty.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Local Minimum — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
